expansion_note: 4 path_escape cases (absolute-path injection past a string-prefix check, Windows UNC/device-namespace bypass of lexical checks, percent-encoded traversal decoded after the containment check, check-to-write symlink swap). This historical expansion fixture is retained as provenance; every case and paired expectation is folded into the strict v0 corpus, so the strict v0 gate is the authoritative target.

cases.intent: A report writer that joins user-supplied file names under the scoped output root is handed a fully absolute path (drive letter or leading slash); the containment check validates the string prefix of the unjoined argument, so the join silently discards the root and the write lands outside the sandbox.

On Windows, a UNC or device-namespace path (server share or question-mark prefix form) is passed where a worktree-relative path is expected; naive startswith-root and lexical normalization checks pass because the device namespace skips Win32 path normalization, and the write escapes to a network share outside the sandbox.

A path argument arrives with percent-encoded traversal segments and mixed separators; the containment check runs on the raw string, and only a later layer decodes and normalizes the path, so the decoded dot-dot segments walk out of the sandbox after the check has already passed.

A path passes resolve-and-containment validation, but between the check and the write a directory component is swapped for a symlink pointing outside the worktree, so the time-of-use write follows the new link and escapes the sandbox the check had approved.
